There is evidence of appointment activity and administrative capacity, including women and Christians in senior offices, Sisi’s appointment of judges, anti-trafficking training, and related government programs (BATCH-0002-E015; BATCH-0008-E005; BATCH-0023-E015). These facts show representation and formal or operational activity, but do not establish politically neutral appointments or institutional independence. During the relevant period, policymaking was dominated by the presidency, military, and intelligence agencies; parliament was largely a pro-regime rubber stamp; and Sisi controlled an anticorruption authority assessed as lacking impartiality (BATCH-0008-E001; BATCH-0008-E010; BATCH-0002-E004). The strongest personnel and administrative evidence concerns institutional control beyond ordinary civil-service practice: presidential appointment and security control over university leadership, political exclusions and surveillance in higher education, and military autonomy in civilian project design, licensing, and partner selection (BATCH-0008-E023; BATCH-0009-R10-E001; BATCH-0009-R10-E002). The government also repeatedly postponed opening military companies to private investors, and Sisi allocated new land to the army in early 2023; the evidence suggests reluctance to curtail the military’s role, while also identifying military veto power as a constraint (BATCH-0009-R11-E009; BATCH-0009-R11-E010; BATCH-0009-R11-E011). Thus, the supplied record supports politicized and non-neutral administration, especially in presidential, security, university, and military-linked institutions, but does not by itself establish a general formal loyalty-test policy across the entire civil service or a personality cult.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E015","BATCH-0008-E005","BATCH-0023-E015"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E001","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0008-E023","BATCH-0009-R10-E001","BATCH-0009-R10-E002","BATCH-0009-R11-E009","BATCH-0009-R11-E010","BATCH-0009-R11-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence is stronger for presidential, security, university, and military-linked institutional control than for ordinary civil-service appointments, dismissals, or a comprehensive civil-service rule system.","Appointment and training examples establish representation or administrative inputs, not independence, neutrality, or protection from political pressure after appointment.","The supplied evidence does not establish a general formal loyalty-test policy across all public institutions, nor does it directly document a personality cult.","Some military-governance evidence is analytical or retrospective and does not provide a complete 2023 personnel register or administrative record."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported broad claim that party and security loyalty shaped all public institutions.","Distinguished military delegation and autonomy from evidence about ordinary civil-service politicization.","Preserved the qualified finding that the evidence suggests reluctance to curtail military influence rather than asserting an unqualified general loyalty policy.","Retained favorable appointment, representation, training, and program evidence as qualifying context rather than treating it as proof of institutional neutrality."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
